entity-ungrouped-transition-morphscene-entity-transitions0 of 0.75 (major)failThe requirement is that an entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps animates in place from its old state to its new state. For ungrouped steps this is not met. When two steps don&#39;t share a group, sceneKey returns a different key, so Stage mounts a brand-new Scene. Stage&#39;s sync AnimatePresence does keep both scenes mounted together, and both sit inside one LayoutGroup. But the kit&#39;s primitives that render a persisting entity in the incoming scene still make it vanish and reappear instead of morphing. (1) Arrow. Arrow is a kit entity primitive, and its id is used only as a data-presentation-entity attribute. It has no layoutId and no layout prop. Its paths use morph(d) with initial:false and animate:{d}. A freshly mounted Arrow in the new scene therefore starts at its final geometry, while the old Arrow fades out with the outgoing scene over EXIT_T. Nothing links the two copies, so the arrow does not animate from its old geometry. This is judge A&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. (2) Appear. The kit&#39;s own scene pattern wraps every entity in Appear: the bootstrap template Scene, the delivered SampleScene, and the kit&#39;s stage tests. appearProps gives Appear initial opacity 0 and a default delay of ENTER_DELAY (0.65s). In a fresh scene every Appear mounts again, so the incoming copy of a persisting Box stays at opacity 0 until 0.65s. Its layoutId morph lasts LAYOUT_T (0.6s), so it finishes before the copy becomes visible. Meanwhile the outgoing scene fades to opacity 0 in EXIT_T (0.25s). The guidance names this failure case: both steps stay mounted, but the primitives hide the incoming copy until the outgoing copy has faded. This is judge B&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. Judge C (pass) is correct that the scene wrapper uses sync mode and is absolutely positioned, and that Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip carry a layoutId and no opacity delay. That does not decide the requirement, for three reasons: - The guidance says the mode alone does not establish a pass. - C&#39;s argument ignores Arrow, which has no shared layoutId at all. - C&#39;s argument ignores Appear, the kit wrapper that the kit&#39;s own template and sample put around every entity, which holds the incoming copy at opacity 0 for longer than the outgoing fade. The stage test &#39;cross-fades a replaced scene&#39; only uses different ids (x then z) and checks that elements exist in the DOM. engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exitengineering-verification-tooling-robustness0.625 of 0.625 (major)passI rule with A and B. startPreview (preview.mjs) runs the Vite binary directly with process.execPath. It does not go through an npm or npx wrapper, so the server is the spawned child itself. The child is spawned detached, and stop() sends SIGTERM to its whole process group (process.kill(-child.pid)). It then awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, raced against a 2s timer, and sends SIGKILL to the group if the timer wins. If readiness fails inside startPreview, stop() is called before the error is rethrown. teardown() closes the browser in a try and calls preview.stop() in a finally, so the preview is stopped even when browser.close() rejects. In verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, startPreview, chromium.launch() and all later work sit inside one try whose finally awaits teardown({browser, preview}). That covers success, a failing check (a thrown PhaseError), a browser launch failure and any later error. The bootstrap template copies are identical to the repository copies. Judge C says stop() does not await exit after the SIGKILL fallback. That is accurate, but it does not decide the requirement. Arrow is a kit entity primitive, and its id is used only as a data-presentation-entity attribute. It has no layoutId and no layout prop. Its paths use morph(d) with initial:false and animate:{d}. A freshly mounted Arrow in the new scene therefore starts at its final geometry, while the old Arrow fades out with the outgoing scene over EXIT_T. Nothing links the two copies, so the arrow does not animate from its old geometry. This is judge A&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. (2) Appear. The kit&#39;s own scene pattern wraps every entity in Appear: the bootstrap template Scene, the delivered SampleScene, and the kit&#39;s stage tests. appearProps gives Appear initial opacity 0 and a default delay of ENTER_DELAY (0.65s). In a fresh scene every Appear mounts again, so the incoming copy of a persisting Box stays at opacity 0 until 0.65s. Its layoutId morph lasts LAYOUT_T (0.6s), so it finishes before the copy becomes visible. Meanwhile the outgoing scene fades to opacity 0 in EXIT_T (0.25s). The guidance names this failure case: both steps stay mounted, but the primitives hide the incoming copy until the outgoing copy has faded. This is judge B&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. Judge C (pass) is correct that the scene wrapper uses sync mode and is absolutely positioned, and that Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip carry a layoutId and no opacity delay. That does not decide the requirement, for three reasons: - The guidance says the mode alone does not establish a pass. - C&#39;s argument ignores Arrow, which has no shared layoutId at all. - C&#39;s argument ignores Appear, the kit wrapper that the kit&#39;s own template and sample put around every entity, which holds the incoming copy at opacity 0 for longer than the outgoing fade. The stage test &#39;cross-fades a replaced scene&#39; only uses different ids (x then z) and checks that elements exist in the DOM. tiebreaks{"demo-integration":null,"scene-kit":{"ok":true,"criteria":["entity-ungrouped-transition-morph"],"inventory_kind":"neutral source","attempts":[{"stage":"tiebreak","attempt":1,"ok":true,"error":null}],"first_results":[{"id":"entity-ungrouped-transition-morph","verdict":"fail","rationale":"The requirement is that an entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps animates in place from its old state to its new state. For ungrouped steps this is not met. When two steps don&#39;t share a group, sceneKey returns a different key, so Stage mounts a brand-new Scene. Stage&#39;s sync AnimatePresence does keep both scenes mounted together, and both sit inside one LayoutGroup. But the kit&#39;s primitives that render a persisting entity in the incoming scene still make it vanish and reappear instead of morphing. (1) Arrow. Arrow is a kit entity primitive, and its id is used only as a data-presentation-entity attribute. It has no layoutId and no layout prop. Its paths use morph(d) with initial:false and animate:{d}. A freshly mounted Arrow in the new scene therefore starts at its final geometry, while the old Arrow fades out with the outgoing scene over EXIT_T. Nothing links the two copies, so the arrow does not animate from its old geometry. This is judge A&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. (2) Appear. The kit&#39;s own scene pattern wraps every entity in Appear: the bootstrap template Scene, the delivered SampleScene, and the kit&#39;s stage tests. appearProps gives Appear initial opacity 0 and a default delay of ENTER_DELAY (0.65s). In a fresh scene every Appear mounts again, so the incoming copy of a persisting Box stays at opacity 0 until 0.65s. Its layoutId morph lasts LAYOUT_T (0.6s), so it finishes before the copy becomes visible. Meanwhile the outgoing scene fades to opacity 0 in EXIT_T (0.25s). The guidance names this failure case: both steps stay mounted, but the primitives hide the incoming copy until the outgoing copy has faded. This is judge B&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. Judge C (pass) is correct that the scene wrapper uses sync mode and is absolutely positioned, and that Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip carry a layoutId and no opacity delay. That does not decide the requirement, for three reasons: - The guidance says the mode alone does not establish a pass. - C&#39;s argument ignores Arrow, which has no shared layoutId at all. - C&#39;s argument ignores Appear, the kit wrapper that the kit&#39;s own template and sample put around every entity, which holds the incoming copy at opacity 0 for longer than the outgoing fade. The stage test &#39;cross-fades a replaced scene&#39; only uses different ids (x then z) and checks that elements exist in the DOM. consecutive steps animates in place from its old state to its new state. For ungrouped steps this is not met. When two steps don&#39;t share a group, sceneKey returns a different key, so Stage mounts a brand-new Scene. Stage&#39;s sync AnimatePresence does keep both scenes mounted together, and both sit inside one LayoutGroup. But the kit&#39;s primitives that render a persisting entity in the incoming scene still make it vanish and reappear instead of morphing. (1) Arrow. Arrow is a kit entity primitive, and its id is used only as a data-presentation-entity attribute. It has no layoutId and no layout prop. Its paths use morph(d) with initial:false and animate:{d}. A freshly mounted Arrow in the new scene therefore starts at its final geometry, while the old Arrow fades out with the outgoing scene over EXIT_T. Nothing links the two copies, so the arrow does not animate from its old geometry. This is judge A&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. (2) Appear. The kit&#39;s own scene pattern wraps every entity in Appear: the bootstrap template Scene, the delivered SampleScene, and the kit&#39;s stage tests. appearProps gives Appear initial opacity 0 and a default delay of ENTER_DELAY (0.65s). In a fresh scene every Appear mounts again, so the incoming copy of a persisting Box stays at opacity 0 until 0.65s. Its layoutId morph lasts LAYOUT_T (0.6s), so it finishes before the copy becomes visible. Meanwhile the outgoing scene fades to opacity 0 in EXIT_T (0.25s). The guidance names this failure case: both steps stay mounted, but the primitives hide the incoming copy until the outgoing copy has faded. This is judge B&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. Judge C (pass) is correct that the scene wrapper uses sync mode and is absolutely positioned, and that Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip carry a layoutId and no opacity delay. That does not decide the requirement, for three reasons: - The guidance says the mode alone does not establish a pass. - C&#39;s argument ignores Arrow, which has no shared layoutId at all. - C&#39;s argument ignores Appear, the kit wrapper that the kit&#39;s own template and sample put around every entity, which holds the incoming copy at opacity 0 for longer than the outgoing fade. The stage test &#39;cross-fades a replaced scene&#39; only uses different ids (x then z) and checks that elements exist in the DOM. Stage&#39;s sync AnimatePresence does keep both scenes mounted together, and both sit inside one LayoutGroup. But the kit&#39;s primitives that render a persisting entity in the incoming scene still make it vanish and reappear instead of morphing. (1) Arrow. Arrow is a kit entity primitive, and its id is used only as a data-presentation-entity attribute. It has no layoutId and no layout prop. Its paths use morph(d) with initial:false and animate:{d}. A freshly mounted Arrow in the new scene therefore starts at its final geometry, while the old Arrow fades out with the outgoing scene over EXIT_T. Nothing links the two copies, so the arrow does not animate from its old geometry. This is judge A&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. (2) Appear. In a fresh scene every Appear mounts again, so the incoming copy of a persisting Box stays at opacity 0 until 0.65s. Its layoutId morph lasts LAYOUT_T (0.6s), so it finishes before the copy becomes visible. Meanwhile the outgoing scene fades to opacity 0 in EXIT_T (0.25s). The guidance names this failure case: both steps stay mounted, but the primitives hide the incoming copy until the outgoing copy has faded. This is judge B&#39;s reason, and the source bears it out. The test asserts exactly one overlap warning, that it starts with `WARN step 1 overlap:`, and that it contains both &#39;First label&#39; and &#39;Second label&#39;. They are not collected one by one, but the textless progress indicator that holds them is collected through `[data-presentation-progress]`. talk.css makes that a flex container sized to its dots, so a collision with a dot also hits the progress indicator and is reported with a stable hook label. It does not go through an npm or npx wrapper, so the server is the spawned child itself. The child is spawned detached, and stop() sends SIGTERM to its whole process group (process.kill(-child.pid)). It then awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, raced against a 2s timer, and sends SIGKILL to the group if the timer wins. If readiness fails inside startPreview, stop() is called before the error is rethrown. teardown() closes the browser in a try and calls preview.stop() in a finally, so the preview is stopped even when browser.close() rejects. In verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, startPreview, chromium.launch() and all later work sit inside one try whose finally awaits teardown({browser, preview}). That covers success, a failing check (a thrown PhaseError), a browser launch failure and any later error. The bootstrap template copies are identical to the repository copies. Judge C says stop() does not await exit after the SIGKILL fallback. That is accurate, but it does not decide the requirement. It does not go through an npm or npx wrapper, so the server is the spawned child itself. The child is spawned detached, and stop() sends SIGTERM to its whole process group (process.kill(-child.pid)). It then awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, raced against a 2s timer, and sends SIGKILL to the group if the timer wins. If readiness fails inside startPreview, stop() is called before the error is rethrown. teardown() closes the browser in a try and calls preview.stop() in a finally, so the preview is stopped even when browser.close() rejects. In verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, startPreview, chromium.launch() and all later work sit inside one try whose finally awaits teardown({browser, preview}). That covers success, a failing check (a thrown PhaseError), a browser launch failure and any later error. The bootstrap template copies are identical to the repository copies. Judge C says stop() does not await exit after the SIGKILL fallback. That is accurate, but it does not decide the requirement. The fallback only runs when the server ignores SIGTERM for 2s, which is not one of the exit paths the guidance names. SIGKILL cannot be caught, so the server process is still terminated. On every named path, stop() reaches the server itself and awaits its exit.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:51-55 spawns process.execPath with vite/bin/vite.js &#39;preview&#39; (no npm or npx wrapper) and detached:true.","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:69-82 stop(): signalGroup(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;) on -child.pid, awaits the &#39;exit&#39; promise in Promise.race, SIGKILL on timeout.","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:83-88 stops the child when readiness fails; lines 38-44: teardown runs try { browser.close() } finally { preview.stop() }.","scripts/verify.mjs:111-127 and scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:95-123: startPreview, chromium.launch and all work sit inside try { } finally { await teardown({ browser, preview }) }.","The bootstrap copies skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs, verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs contain the same code at the same lines."],"citations":[{"path":"scripts/lib/preview.mjs","start_line":37,"end_line":90},{"path":"scripts/verify.mjs","start_line":109,"end_line":135},{"path":"scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","start_line":86,"end_line":129},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs","start_line":37,"end_line":90},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","start_line":109,"end_line":135},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","start_line":86,"end_line":129}],"search_scope":[],"missing_obligation":""},{"id":"engineering-tests-isolate-resources","verdict":"fail","rationale":"The requirement has two parts: ports are allocated dynamically, and every test terminates every process it starts. The port part is met: startPreview uses `port ?? (await freePort())`, and freePort listens on port 0. The termination part is not met in tests/e2e/morph-stability.test.mjs. In sampleAdvance, line 41 `const preview = await startPreview(app)` resolves only after the Vite preview is running and ready (preview.mjs lines 83-89). Line 42 `const browser = await chromium.launch()` then runs outside the try block, which only opens at line 43. teardown({ browser, preview }) sits in the finally at lines 62-64, so it covers only the code inside that try. If launch rejects, the finally never runs and nothing calls the preview&#39;s stop(). That launch step is the browser launch this criterion covers, and it is a real exit path of the test&#39;s own code, not an invented input. The test&#39;s only other cleanup is afterAll at line 16, which just removes the temp directory and never stops a preview. The preview is spawned with `detached: true` and `stdio: &#39;ignore&#39;` (preview.mjs lines 51-55), so it runs in its own process group and is not taken down when the test exits. On that path a server the test started is left running, so the &#39;terminate every process they start&#39; clause fails. This failure is about cleanup ordering in the test code; it does not score a missing browser installation. Judges A and B said morph-stability &#39;uses try/finally teardown&#39;. That is true only for code after the browser launch. repository copies and the bootstrap template copies. - **No wrapper:** startPreview spawns the Vite binary directly with process.execPath, so the spawned child is the preview server itself. - **Termination:** the child is detached. stop() sends SIGTERM to its whole process group, awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, and sends SIGKILL to the group if the server has not exited within 2s. - **Readiness failure:** if readiness fails inside startPreview, stop() runs before the error is rethrown. - **Browser close rejects:** teardown() still awaits preview.stop() in a finally block. - **verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs:** startPreview, chromium.launch() and all later work sit inside one try. Its finally awaits teardown({browser, preview}). That covers success, a failing check (a PhaseError), a browser launch failure and any later error. process.exit(1) runs only in main().catch, after that finally has finished. - **Template copies:** they are quoted line for line and are identical. After the SIGKILL fallback, stop() does not await exit. That only matters if the server ignores SIGTERM for 2s, which the guidance does not name as an exit path, and SIGKILL still terminates the server.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:51-55 spawn(process.execPath, [viteBin, &#39;preview&#39;, ...], { detached: true }): the server is the child itself, with no npm/npx wrapper.","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:69-82 stop() sends SIGTERM to the process group (process.kill(-child.pid)), awaits &#39;exit&#39; raced against 2s, then sends SIGKILL.","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:83-88 a readiness failure calls stop() before rethrowing.","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:38-44 teardown awaits preview.stop() in a finally block even if browser.close() rejects.","scripts/verify.mjs:113-127 startPreview, chromium.launch and the checks are inside a try whose finally awaits teardown.","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:97-123 startPreview, chromium.launch and the captures are inside a try whose finally awaits teardown.","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs, verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs: the quoted spans are identical to the repository copies."],"citations":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs"],"marker":"","scope_repair":[],"criterion":"engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exit","cycle":"initial","part":0},{"id":"engineering-tests-isolate-resources","classification":"insufficient","rationale":"The claim&#39;s only counterexample needs chromium.launch() to reject between startPreview (line 41) and the try block (line 43). The quoted material does not show that this happens. The most plausible cause would be a missing browser installation, and this criterion&#39;s guidance says that is not scored here. On the paths the material does establish, the test stops what it starts: - **Port:** sampleAdvance calls startPreview(app) with no port, so freePort() picks one dynamically. - **Server:** the spawned child is the Vite server itself, not an npx wrapper. - **Cleanup:** teardown runs in a finally block that stops both the browser and the preview. It does not go through an npm or npx wrapper, so the server is the spawned child itself. The child is spawned detached, and stop() sends SIGTERM to its whole process group (process.kill(-child.pid)). It then awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, raced against a 2s timer, and sends SIGKILL to the group if the timer wins. If readiness fails inside startPreview, stop() is called before the error is rethrown. teardown() closes the browser in a try and calls preview.stop() in a finally, so the preview is stopped even when browser.close() rejects. In verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, startPreview, chromium.launch() and all later work sit inside one try whose finally awaits teardown({browser, preview}). That covers success, a failing check (a thrown PhaseError), a browser launch failure and any later error. The bootstrap template copies are identical to the repository copies. Judge C says stop() does not await exit after the SIGKILL fallback. That is accurate, but it does not decide the requirement. The fallback only runs when the server ignores SIGTERM for 2s, which is not one of the exit paths the guidance names. SIGKILL cannot be caught, so the server process is still terminated. In sampleAdvance, line 41 `const preview = await startPreview(app)` resolves only after the Vite preview is running and ready (preview.mjs lines 83-89). Line 42 `const browser = await chromium.launch()` then runs outside the try block, which only opens at line 43. teardown({ browser, preview }) sits in the finally at lines 62-64, so it covers only the code inside that try. If launch rejects, the finally never runs and nothing calls the preview&#39;s stop(). That launch step is the browser launch this criterion covers, and it is a real exit path of the test&#39;s own code, not an invented input. The test&#39;s only other cleanup is afterAll at line 16, which just removes the temp directory and never stops a preview. The preview is spawned with `detached: true` and `stdio: &#39;ignore&#39;` (preview.mjs lines 51-55), so it runs in its own process group and is not taken down when the test exits. On that path a server the test started is left running, so the &#39;terminate every process they start&#39; clause fails. This failure is about cleanup ordering in the test code; it does not score a missing browser installation. Judges A and B said morph-stability &#39;uses try/finally teardown&#39;. That is true only for code after the browser launch. Their own citations show startPreview and chromium.launch both run before the try, so their reason does not establish that every started process is terminated. Their other points, freePort and the verify-success and verify-failures leftover checks, concern other files and the port clause. They do not cure this test. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[{"id":"entity-ungrouped-transition-morph","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The auditor&#39;s reading matches the material, and the review guidance treats it as a failure. Stage.tsx uses AnimatePresence in its default sync mode, and each scene is absolutely positioned, so both steps&#39; scenes stay mounted together. On an ungrouped transition, sceneKey changes, so a new Scene instance mounts. Every Appear inside it mounts fresh. Appear is a kit primitive in presentation-kit/nodes. Both the sample and the kit&#39;s own tests wrap every Box in it. appearProps gives Appear initial opacity 0 and a default delay of ENTER_DELAY = 0.65s, followed by a 0.4s fade. Meanwhile the outgoing scene wrapper fades to opacity 0 over EXIT_T = 0.25s. The incoming Box shares its layoutId with the outgoing one, so its layout morph runs for LAYOUT_T = 0.6s. That morph runs inside an ancestor held at opacity 0 until 0.65s, and it is finished before the entity becomes visible. So the persisting entity disappears with the fading outgoing scene and reappears at its new position. It does not stay visible while it moves. The guidance names this case: both steps are kept mounted, but the entity primitives hide the incoming copy until the outgoing copy has faded. The guidance also requires that the persisting entity stay visible while it animates, and that the mode alone does not establish a pass. The primary pass checked only Box/useEntityMotion and missed the Appear wrapper that renders the persisting entity. The &#39;cross-fades a replaced scene&#39; test uses different ids (x → z) and checks only DOM presence. It does not show a persisting entity staying visible across an ungrouped transition.","evidence":["Stage.tsx: &lt;AnimatePresence&gt; with no mode, so the default sync mode applies. Each scene is a motion.div keyed by sceneKey(step), absolutely positioned, with exit opacity 0 over EXIT_T.","constants.ts: EXIT_T = 0.25, LAYOUT_T = 0.6, ENTER_DELAY = 0.65, ENTER_T = 0.4.","appearProps.ts: initial { opacity: 0 }, animate { opacity: 1 }, transition { duration: ENTER_T, delay (default ENTER_DELAY) }.","Appear.tsx (kit nodes) applies appearProps on mount. A newly mounted scene after an ungrouped transition remounts every Appear.","SampleScene.tsx wraps every entity in &lt;Appear&gt; inside SceneLayer. CountingScene in stage.test.tsx does the same around Box.","entity.ts: the layout transition is LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, which ends before the 0.65s Appear delay does, so the morph runs while the incoming copy is invisible.","stage.test.tsx &#39;cross-fades a replaced scene&#39; uses entity x then z and checks only DOM presence, not that a persisting entity stays visible."],"citations":["src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx","src/presentation-kit/constants.ts","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Appear.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/appearProps.ts","src/presentation-kit/nodes/entity.ts","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/SampleScene.tsx","src/presentation-kit/__tests__/stage.test.tsx"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":0,"sample":1}],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[{"id":"verification-step-error-fails","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The auditor&#39;s reading of the source is right: at index 0 the verifier never reads data-step-index. That does not break the criterion. The review guidance says the verifier must not treat a missing or non-numeric hook as progress. It names two failure modes: a transition check that turns an absent or non-numeric hook into a number that still passes its comparison (such as Number(null) === 0), and an unreadable step count that makes the verifier step through nothing and still pass. Neither happens here. Step 0 is the initial state, not an advance, so no progress is credited and no comparison passes on a coerced value. Every real transition goes through waitForStepIndex, which compares getAttribute(...) === String(want) as strings. A null or non-numeric index can never match a positive step, so a missing or garbage index fails the first transition. The step count is checked with !(count &gt;= 1), so NaN, 0, or a missing count fails instead of stepping through nothing. The auditor&#39;s one-step case is a hypothetical input: the candidate&#39;s sample has nine steps, and the guidance does not name that scenario. The required executable evidence also exists: tests for a render exception at a later step and for a stuck transition both assert a non-zero exit and name the offending step.","evidence":["scripts/lib/browse.mjs waitForStepIndex compares `getAttribute(&#39;data-step-index&#39;) === String(want)`. A missing attribute gives null, which never equals &#39;1&#39;..&#39;8&#39;, so a missing …","scripts/verify.mjs: `if (!(count &gt;= 1)) throw new PhaseError(&#39;render&#39;, `invalid step count ...`)`, so a missing, zero, or NaN step count fails instead of stepping through no steps.","scripts/verify.mjs only presses ArrowRight and waits for the index when index &gt; 0. Step 0 is the initial render, not a transition, so nothing is counted as progress there.","tests/e2e/verify-failures.test.mjs &#39;fails when a component throws while rendering a later step&#39; asserts a non-zero exit and `FAIL [render] .* at step 5`. &#39;fails when a transition does not…","The one-step case the auditor raises is a hypothetical input. The candidate&#39;s reference sample has nine steps, and the guidance does not name that scenario."],"citations":["scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/lib/browse.mjs","tests/e2e/verify-failures.test.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"engineering-quality":[],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
